message.content:
Explore /home/krubics/.config/waybar thoroughly.

I need to understand:
1. All jsonc config files and where image modules (modules of type "image", i.e. `"image#something"` or `"image"`) are defined. List each one with its full config block (path, size, interval, exec, etc).
2. The "pokeball" example — find how it is implemented. The user says pokeball uses a CSS background-image instead of a waybar image module. Find that CSS rule and the corresponding module (probably a custom module or a label) in the jsonc.
3. All CSS files and the relevant style rules for image modules and the pokeball module.
4. Any scripts referenced by these modules (exec paths), and what they output.
5. The image asset files/directories used (e.g. pokemon sprites), their formats and dimensions if discoverable.

Be very thorough. Report back with full file paths and verbatim config/CSS snippets so I can plan a conversion of all image modules to CSS background-image based modules.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Emits a divider glyph only when the given monitor's active workspace has
# open windows, so the divider disappears entirely (no reserved space)
# alongside the native workspace-taskbar icons when the workspace is empty.
set -euo pipefail
MONITOR="${1:-$WAYBAR_OUTPUT_NAME}"

emit() {
  local ws count
  ws=$(hyprctl -j monitors | jq -r --arg m "$MONITOR" '.[] | select(.name == $m) | .activeWorkspace.id')
  count=$(hyprctl -j clients | jq -r --argjson ws "${ws:-0}" '[ .[] | select(.workspace.id == $ws) ] | length')
  if [ "${count:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
    jq -nc '{text: "│"}'
  else
    jq -nc '{text: ""}'
  fi
}

emit

socat -U - "UNIX-CONNECT:$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hypr/$HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE/.socket2.sock" | \
while read -r line; do
  case "$line" in
    openwindow*|closewindow*|movewindow*|workspace*|activewindow*|focusedmon*)
      emit
      ;;
  esac
done

I now have a complete picture. Here is my thorough report.

## 1. JSONC config files

There is exactly one config file: `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/config.jsonc`. (`/home/krubics/.config/waybar/.vscode/settings.json` exists but is editor config, not waybar config.)

### Image modules defined (all in `config.jsonc`)

There are **4 image modules**, all referenced in `modules-left`/`modules-right`:

**`image#clock`** (lines 64-67):
```jsonc
"image#clock": {
  "path": "/home/krubics/.config/waybar/images/dialga.png",
  "size": 32,
},
```

**`image#network`** (lines 69-72):
```jsonc
"image#network": {
  "path": "/home/krubics/.config/waybar/images/pixelated-wooper.png",
  "size": 32,
},
```

**`image#bluetooth`** (lines 88-91):
```jsonc
"image#bluetooth": {
  "path": "/home/krubics/.config/waybar/images/pixelated-magneton.png",
  "size": 32,
},
```

**`image#battery`** (lines 97-101) — this one is dynamic, using `exec` instead of a static `path`:
```jsonc
"image#battery": {
  "exec": "/home/krubics/.config/waybar/scripts/pickachu-battery.sh",
  "size": 115,
  "interval": 30,
},
```

Module placement (lines 7-26): `image#clock` is at the far left before the clock; `image#network`, `image#bluetooth`, and `image#battery` are on the right, each paired with its text module (`network`, `bluetooth`, `battery`). Note `image#battery` sits *after* the `battery` text module (line 24-25), whereas the other image modules sit *before* their text module.

## 2. The "pokeball" example

The pokeball is **not** a waybar image module. It is a CSS `background-image` applied to the active workspace button of the `hyprland/workspaces` module.

- The waybar module is `hyprland/workspaces` (config lines 28-33), placed in `modules-center` (line 13). Its `format` is `"{name}"` — it renders the workspace name/number as a normal label. There is no custom module or `image` module for the pokeball.
- The CSS rule is in `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/style.css`, lines 22-35:

```css
/* :not(.taskbar) keeps this off the taskbar module's active button */
#workspaces:not(.taskbar) button.active {
    background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pixelated-pokeball.png');
    background-position: center;
    background-repeat: no-repeat;
    background-size: contain;
    background-origin: content-box; /* inset the ball from the accent pill's edges */
    background-color: #89b4fa;
    color: transparent; /* hides the workspace number behind the pokeball */
    padding: 2px 2px;
    min-width: 22px;
    min-height: 22px;
    margin: 4px 0px;
    border-radius: 5px;
}
```

Key technique for the conversion: waybar/GTK CSS supports `background-image: url(...)` with `background-size: contain`, `background-position: center`, `background-repeat: no-repeat`, and the button/label is sized via `min-width`/`min-height` (plus `padding`). `color: transparent` hides the underlying text label. This is the exact pattern you'd replicate to convert the `image#*` modules into CSS-backed label/custom modules.

## 3. CSS files and relevant rules

Only one CSS file: `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/style.css` (61 lines total).

- **No existing style rules target the image modules** (`#image`, `#clock` image, etc.). The `image#*` modules render their PNGs natively via waybar's image widget, so they have no CSS. This means after conversion you will need to *add* new CSS rules for each converted module.
- The `clock` rule: note there is a text `clock` module but no `#clock` CSS rule — the `#clock` selector is currently unused, and `image#clock` has no selector. (Be careful: if you convert `image#clock` to a custom/label module, GTK widget names may collide — waybar names the image module widget `#image` by default, or `#clock` if you match the id.)
- Global rule (lines 1-5) sets font and `background: none` on everything.
- Container rules (lines 12-19): `.modules-left/.center/.right` get a semi-transparent pill background.
- Pokeball rule (lines 22-35, quoted above).
- Divider rules (lines 37-41): `#custom-taskbar-divider, #custom-divider`.
- Taskbar rules (lines 43-60): `#workspaces.taskbar button` and `.taskbar-window`.

## 4. Scripts referenced by modules

Two scripts in `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/scripts/`:

**`pickachu-battery.sh`** — referenced by `image#battery` `exec`. It reads `/sys/class/power_supply/BAT0/capacity` and echoes a single PNG path (absolute) depending on the battery level (>80, >60, >40, >20, >10, else). Output is a bare file path string (what `image` module `exec` expects), e.g. `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/images/100-percent-pikachu.png`.

**IMPORTANT — broken path references in this script** (relevant to your conversion, since a CSS approach would use classes tied to level buckets rather than emitting paths). The script echoes filenames that do not all match the actual files on disk:
- Echoes `80-percent-pikachu.png` → actual file is `80-percent-pickachu.png` (note "pi**ck**achu"). MISMATCH.
- Echoes `60-percent-pikachu.png` → actual file is `60-percent-pika**chi**.png`. MISMATCH.
- Echoes `10-percent-pikachu.png` → actual file is `10-percent-pi**ck**achu.png`. MISMATCH.
- `100-`, `40-`, `20-` percent names match correctly.

So 3 of the 6 battery sprites are currently broken references. When converting to CSS you will map battery ranges to CSS classes; note the on-disk filenames when writing `url(...)`.

**`workspace-tabs.sh`** — referenced by `custom/taskbar-divider` `exec` (return-type json). Unrelated to images; it emits a `│` divider glyph as JSON `{text: ...}` based on whether the active workspace has windows, and subscribes to the Hyprland socket for live updates. Not relevant to the image conversion.

## 5. Image assets

Two directories:

`/home/krubics/.config/waybar/images/` (used by image modules):
| File | Format | Dimensions | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dialga.png` | PNG RGBA 8-bit | 800 x 800 | `image#clock` |
| `pixelated-wooper.png` | PNG 4-bit colormap | 256 x 256 | `image#network` |
| `pixelated-magneton.png` | PNG RGBA 8-bit | 364 x 364 | `image#bluetooth` |
| `100-percent-pikachu.png` | PNG RGBA 8-bit | 677 x 200 | battery script (>80) |
| `80-percent-pickachu.png` | PNG RGBA 8-bit | 677 x 200 | battery (>60) — name mismatch |
| `60-percent-pikachi.png` | PNG RGBA 8-bit | 677 x 200 | battery (>40) — name mismatch |
| `40-percent-pikachu.png` | PNG RGBA 8-bit | 677 x 200 | battery (>20) |
| `20-percent-pikachu.png` | PNG RGBA 8-bit | 677 x 200 | battery (>10) |
| `10-percent-pickachu.png` | PNG RGBA 8-bit | 677 x 200 | battery (else) — name mismatch |

`/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/` (used by CSS):
| File | Format | Dimensions | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pixelated-pokeball.png` | PNG RGBA 8-bit | 512 x 512 | pokeball CSS rule (`button.active`) |

Note the battery sprites are non-square (677 x 200, aspect ~3.4:1), which is why `image#battery` uses a large `size: 115` — worth accounting for `background-size`/aspect-ratio when converting to CSS (`contain` will letterbox within the label box). The other icons are square.

## Summary for your conversion plan
- 4 image modules to convert: `image#clock`, `image#network`, `image#bluetooth` (static `path`), and `image#battery` (dynamic `exec` script → needs a level-class approach in CSS).
- The proven CSS pattern already exists in the pokeball rule (`style.css` lines 22-35): `background-image: url(...)` + `background-size: contain` + `background-repeat/position` + `min-width/min-height` + `color: transparent`.
- All CSS lives in one file: `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/style.css`; you'll add new selectors (currently none target the image modules).
- Watch the 3 broken battery filename references in `pickachu-battery.sh` and the non-square battery sprite aspect ratio.
